comments.body:
## Cross-reference: this may be the same bug as a89d, whose premise it contradicts

Open ticket a89d-4dd2-f421-417a is titled "Completion verifier exhausts its turn budget on
genuine breadth, NOT on a loop", and cites tickets 9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56 and db1c-2a74-ffe1-4f90
hitting the same wall.

The measurement behind THIS bug (max_consecutive_repeat=131 on one identical `search_files`
signature out of 260 calls, failing identically at REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=1200) is direct evidence
of a loop. Two possibilities, undetermined:

- a89d's premise is wrong and these are ONE bug — in which case one of the two should close as
  duplicate, and a89d's ACs 1-4 are aimed at the wrong target.
- There are TWO distinct exhaustion modes — genuine breadth and non-progressing loop — in which
  case these are siblings and a89d should be re-scoped to the former.

The cheap discriminator: re-run 9fd4 and db1c now that a89d's repetition telemetry exists (it
landed as commit 5f00bf5253 and is what produced the 131 figure). If those cases show low repeat
counts, both modes are real. If they show high ones, it is one bug.

Worth noting the telemetry that measured this was built BY a89d — its instrument has now
characterised a mode its own title excludes.

UNVERIFIED LEAD: the looping call is `search_files`, and commit 85805e02f1 ("bf31: search_files
must not fake '(no matches)'") changed that tool today. Whether an honest empty result alters
retry behaviour is untested speculation — check before believing it.

comments.body: Consolidating into epic 9b71-55b3-1bd1-4a97 (completion gate loop breaker) — this scenario is covered, with one important design correction. Your detection proposal (consecutive-repeat threshold, default 5) is the exact metric ticket 70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0 proved INVERTED on real traces: a k-cycle with k>=2 never repeats adjacently (bf31's 4-call cycle repeated 31-37x scores max_consecutive_repeat=1), and the HEALTHY 258-call run scores 5 — your default threshold sits exactly on the healthy run's value. The adopted detector is a windowed distinct-ratio (distinct_ratio_window, window 24, trip <=0.50, order-insensitive): your 131x adjacent case craters it to ~0.04 (fires within ~24 calls), and it also catches the cycles adjacency misses, never firing on the healthy profile (min w24 ratio 0.833). Your actuator (stop + distinct message) is subsumed by c827's adopted route: typed RunawayToolLoopError -> classified ahead of the provider-outage sweep -> bounded per-criterion recovery + tool-free finalizer, so the run ends with a VERDICT where possible, and a gate_error_v1 sidecar naming the loop (not 'raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS') where not. Your requests=240 tool_calls=260 distinct=120 max_consecutive_repeat=131 trace is a valuable third pathological test vector (adjacent-repeat mode) and is being pinned in the detector tests alongside the 4-cycle and the healthy control. 94a3-1323-3497-4f59 (in_progress, merged, 17 ACs, blocked only by this gate defect) is noted as the ready-made live verification case for the epic. Also for the record: 4 of 5 measured pathological runs LOOPED on search_files AFTER the 85805e02f1 fix landed, so the loop mode does not depend on the pre-fix lying tool.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Closing bug 94a3-1323-3497-4f59 failed twice on the completion-verification gate, at
`REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` of both 480 (the default) and 1200. Both runs died the same way:

    step 'decide@then/verify' failed: agent exceeded its step budget
    (max_iterations=480; ~1 model request per tool call)

The telemetry shows this is a LOOP, not an under-sized budget. From the 480-step run:

    requests=240 tool_calls=260 distinct=120 max_consecutive_repeat=131
    top_repeats=[{'signature': 'search_files:831f8022', 'count': 132}, ...]

131 CONSECUTIVE repeats of one identical `search_files` call, out of 260 total tool calls —
more than half the budget spent re-issuing a single byte-identical query. Raising the budget
to 1200 simply let it loop longer and fail again, which is the diagnostic: a budget increase
cannot fix a non-progressing loop.

The user-visible cost is that a legitimately complete ticket cannot be closed through the
gate. The only escape the error names is `--force-close`, which discards the completion
attestation entirely — so an infrastructure loop silently pushes authors toward bypassing a
safety gate, which is exactly the wrong lesson.

## Approach

Short-circuit non-progressing repetition in the agentic runner: track a signature of each tool
call (the runner already computes one — the `search_files:831f8022` form appears in the
existing step-budget telemetry) and, when the same signature repeats consecutively beyond a
small threshold, stop the agent and return a distinct, actionable outcome rather than letting
it burn to the step ceiling.

Two parts:

1. Detect and stop. The consecutive-repeat counter already exists for telemetry
   (`max_consecutive_repeat`); promote it to a control signal with a configurable threshold
   (default small, e.g. 5 — well above legitimate retry-with-backoff, far below 131).
2. Report it distinctly. A loop must NOT surface as "exceeded its step budget ... Raise
   REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS", because that advice is wrong for a loop and the author will follow it
   and lose another ten minutes. It needs its own message naming the repeated call and saying
   that raising the budget will not help.

Why this rather than just raising the default budget: the observed failure is unbounded
repetition, so no finite ceiling fixes it — it only changes how long the author waits before
the same error. Detecting non-progress is the smallest change that turns an infinite class of
failure into a bounded, correctly-explained one.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/` — the agentic runner that enforces `max_iterations` and already records
  `max_consecutive_repeat` / `top_repeats` in its step-budget telemetry; add the threshold
  check and the distinct outcome there.
- `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — the close-gate message that currently renders the
  step-budget remedy; render the loop outcome's own remedy when that is the cause.
- `tests/unit/` — the tests below.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — document the loop guard and its threshold.

## Testing

- Happy path: a fake runner that returns the same tool-call signature repeatedly is stopped at
  the threshold, not at `max_iterations`.
- Edge: a runner that repeats a signature fewer times than the threshold, interleaved with
  progress, runs to completion and is NOT stopped.
- Failure path: the resulting close-gate error names the repeated call and does not advise
  raising `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An agentic step whose tool-call signature repeats consecutively beyond the threshold is
      stopped at that point; verified by a test asserting the run ends after threshold+1 calls
      rather than after `max_iterations`.
- [ ] A run that repeats a signature below the threshold, with progress in between, still
      completes normally; verified by a test.
- [ ] The loop outcome is reported distinctly from a genuine budget exhaustion and does NOT
      advise raising `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`; verified by a test asserting the message contains
      the repeated call's name and not that advice.
- [ ] The threshold is configurable and defaults to a value below 10; verified by a test
      reading the default.
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` documents the loop guard; verified by a grep.

## Provenance

Reproduced twice on 94a3-1323-3497-4f59 while closing it after its change merged
(Gerrit 1434). The ticket could not be closed through the gate and `--force-close` was
deliberately NOT used.
